subject: Why all the reported bases and promoter regions are from negative strand?

messages.author: 281bf392d852a6b2
messages.subject: Why all the reported bases and promoter regions are from negative strand?
parts:
Hi,
I have RRBS data from Illumina HiSeq. I used Bismark to  map to genome. I used sam files from Bismakr in methylKit. All the methylated bases and promoters reported by methykit are from negative strand. Is it a problem? If yes, what could be cause of this problem ?

I apprecaite your comments. Thanks !

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Why all the reported bases and promoter regions are from negative strand?
parts: It could be a bismark problem or your alignment settings. I have never seen such a case, someone in the group might have seen it. In any case, you should look for the problem upstream of methylkit first. Contact again if you are 100% sure if it is related to methylkit

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Why all the reported bases and promoter regions are from negative strand?
parts:
The problem does not seem to be in bismark, because there are alignment on both the strands. In one of the bismark output sam files there are 3530182 reads aligned to positive strand and 3643055 reads aligned to negative strand.

I imported SAM files using read.bismark() function and assigned it to meth.raw. When I checked the strand information from meth.raw there is not a single base that has methylation on positive strand. Is this expected?

messages.author: e4181d5c40fc094c
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Why all the reported bases and promoter regions are from negative strand?
parts:
I have heard a similar thing from my colleague. But when I started troubleshooting it, I noticed that he didn't sort the file in the order of "chr" and "chr start" (He rather used samtools sort and Picard sort). Using unix sort helped him!

previously, I vaguely remember that either the vignette or slides have information of the command that need to be used for sorting. Now I could not find it! You may consider updating the needed command. So that people sort it in the way that is needed!

Regards,
Kalyan
